title: Browser Extensions Can Read What Your Wallet Sees
summary: A browser extension with broad permissions can read and change what you see on the pages you visit. A malicious one can swap the destination address on a transfer page, alter a payment request, or capture what you type into a web wallet.
blocks: A browser extension with broad permissions can read and change what you see on the pages you visit. A malicious one can swap the destination address on a transfer page, alter a payment request, or capture what you type into a web wallet.

Risky extensions rarely announce themselves. Some start honest and turn harmful after being sold to a new owner and silently updated; others imitate a well-known tool with a near-identical name and icon.

Keep the browser you use for wallets and exchanges as bare as possible: install only extensions you truly need, from verified publishers, and review their permissions from time to time. A separate browser profile with no extensions at all is a simple, strong habit for anything involving funds.
